scope: Read-only installed-source and current generated-index inspection; no Sphinx build, source edit, preservation wrapper or timing experiment.
parallel_conclusion: Adding -j4 to this Windows Sphinx8.2.3 process does not enable parallel reading or writing. Both builder branches require parallel_available; the process implementation explicitly requires POSIX fork. Preserve current strict -W --keep-going invocation; no unsupported Windows publisher parallelism change is recommended.

memory_limits.reason: Windows creates no parallel workers by this option. A hypothetical POSIX run can have a parent plus up to N workers, process-local allocations and temporary serialized environments/doctrees. Fork initially shares memory, but copy-on-write does not bound peak private memory. N=4 cannot be certified safe from a2GiB parent and about10GiB free alone; no POSIX build was inspected or measured here.

navigation.reason_inherited_option_not_effective_he: Book theme active sidebar passes theme_collapse_navbar, not theme_collapse_navigation. Likewise max_navbar_depth/show_navbar_depth are the Book theme controls.
navigation.mechanism: Book sidebar calls generate_toctree_html(startdepth=0,collapse=theme_collapse_navbar,maxdepth=theme_max_navbar_depth,titles_only=True,includehidden=True). PyData passes kwargs to Sphinx global toctree before BeautifulSoup. Sphinx _toctree_standard_entry and _toctree_copy omit nested bullet-list branches that are not current ancestors. This removes nodes before HTML generation rather than merely closing details elements.
navigation.retention: Current branch and its ancestor-path siblings plus top-level section entries remain up to existing depth. Changing this HTML theme option neither modifies env.found_docs nor excludes source pages or search entries. Section landing-page toctrees and ordinary links remain independent.
navigation.tradeoff: Users visit an unrelated section landing page to reveal its children instead of expanding the entire unrelated branch in the present page sidebar. Large flat sibling sets remain large on their own section pages (e.g. reference siblings).
navigation.recommendation: A minimal collapse_navbar=True configuration change is a legitimate candidate for rendering and reader-resource improvement, provided a strict representative HTML regression verifies unrelated descendants absent, current branch/root section links present, unchanged published page/search inventory and section-index reachability. Retain -W and all content. No speedup or fullbuild result is claimed.
